research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10570 at 19 FR 6687 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 16, 1954; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 19, 1954 issue. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between The Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars The Pullman Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10570 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10570_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10570_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_f1cbeae2b3.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated November 20, 1954 and a letter of transmittal dated Chicago, Illinois, November 20, 1954; the board states that by stipulation of the parties the time for making the report was extended to November 26, 1954. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking November 20, 1954 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on November 20, 1954 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to December 20, 1954 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet lists earlier unreviewed producer proposals under research/excavator/claude-apollo-2026-10-31, none canonical and with no review attached; this claim was decided independently from the held texts. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

earlier_end_check: Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. independent_command_check: Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation.
